Modding-API

Schlage Dateioptionen und die Skriptklassen der Simulation nach.

Auf dieser Seite

  • Skriptsymbole
  • Dateioptionen
  • Fracht-IDs

Skriptsymbole

Der Index enthält Funktionen, Eigenschaften, Signale, Konstanten und benannte Aufzählungen der Simulations- und Modding-Klassen. Signaturen und Quellcodekommentare sind auf Englisch. Mod definiert die Einstiegspunkte für Skripte. Andere Klassen und Mitglieder mit führendem Unterstrich können sich zwischen Versionen ändern.

Ergebnisse

Keine passenden Symbole gefunden.

  • Sim._check_crashes funcTrains on the same track crash (with realistic blocking): when a train's nose runs into another train, both are wrecked.
    Link zu diesem Eintragfunc _check_crashes() -> void

    Signals are what keeps them apart. Trains in a depot shed or being serviced there are out of the way. Two trains that already overlapped at the last check, or where one has only just appeared (bought onto a busy platform, out of the depot together with another, a game just loaded), are let go until they part: only running into each other counts.

    Rückgabewert
    void
    Deklariert in scripts/sim/sim.gd:298

Data

  • Data.CARGO constwagon: what one wagon holds (30 when not given).
    Link zu diesem Eintragconst CARGODeklariert in scripts/core/data.gd:5
  • Data.INDUSTRY constworkers: the staff it wants each month (RAIL-28, Industry.staffing), processing plants more than mines and farms.
    Link zu diesem Eintragconst INDUSTRY

    A power station makes nothing for staff to raise, so it wants none. The eras rewrite the chains (RAIL-29). takes and makes are what a kind takes and makes when it first appears; never read them (or later) directly, ask accepts / produces (or Industry's own lists, kept up to date with the map's era): - era: the era (index into ERAS) from which it is found on new maps and opens during the game. - later: what it takes and makes as well from a later era on: {era: {"takes": [...], "makes": [...]}}. - retires: the era from which it is on its way out: a mine's output drifts down every year, a customer nobody supplies may close, and no new ones open (IndustryLife). - needs_all: a plant that only works with every input (two or more): it holds what comes until the rest does, and turns each full set into as many units of output (Economy.deliver_to_industries). It is sited near makers of each input (WorldGen.find_site). - builds: a construction site: it takes these totals, then becomes the kind in becomes. count 0: never found on a new map or opened, only made from another (a finished wind farm). site: where it stands: on "land" (when not given), at "sea", on the "coast", or by a "town" (one of the biggest: a printing works, see WorldGen.find_site). Adding a chain: a new kind with its era, or a later entry on an existing one; town cargos go in TOWN_MAKES / TOWN_TAKES. Everything else (stations, AI, the map's chains, the timeline) follows.

    Deklariert in scripts/core/data.gd:48

  • AiPlayer._second_berth funcShips take turns at a berth (RAIL-26).
    Link zu diesem Eintragfunc _second_berth(sim: Sim, fleet: Array) -> void

    A ship seen waiting (thinks are weeks apart, so it waits often) off one of our one-berth docks, where the ship in the berth is waiting for a full load, gets a second dock tile built beside the first, with a berth of its own - but only when the waiting ship has other work there: cargo to unload, or a different cargo to load. Two ships waiting for the same cargo gain nothing from a berth each: they would share it out between them, fill up no sooner, and then sail in convoy with nobody loading in between. Two berths at most, and an oil rig's dock is nobody's to extend.

    Parameter
    • sim: Sim
    • fleet: Array
    Rückgabewert
    void
    Deklariert in scripts/sim/ai_player.gd:1403

  • BuildOps.plan_level static funcLevel the tiles in rect (all their corners) to height, as far as the rules allow.
    Link zu diesem Eintragstatic func plan_level(m: WorldMap, rect: Rect2i, height: int, blocked: Dictionary = {}) -> Dictionary

    Corners move one level at a time - cutting from the top down, then filling from the bottom up - and drag their neighbours along the way plan_terraform does, so edge-adjacent corners never differ by more than one level. A tile that can't change shape (a building, road or track, a bridge or tunnel, water, or a tile in blocked: tile -> reason) pins its corners, and any move that would disturb a pinned corner is left out; the rest of the area is still levelled. Trees on tiles that change shape are cleared. Extra keys: rect, height, corners (Vector2i -> new height), steps (corner moves, each costing Data.COST.terraform), tiles (tiles that change shape), trees (those of them with trees), why (refused tile -> reason; the same tiles are in bad).

    Parameter
    • m: WorldMap
    • rect: Rect2i
    • height: int
    • blocked: Dictionary = {}
    Rückgabewert
    Dictionary
    Ruft auf
    L.t
    Deklariert in scripts/sim/build_ops.gd:723

  • BuildOps.plan_tunnel static funcA tunnel starting at hillside tile a (an incline rising straight ahead).
    Link zu diesem Eintragstatic func plan_tunnel(m: WorldMap, kind: String, a: Vector2i, hint: bool = true) -> Dictionary

    It runs into the hill to the first tile where the ground comes back down to the entrance's height (tunnel_exit), and that tile is the far mouth. A hill seldom ends in a slope exactly like the one it started with - it comes down on a slant, or one corner sticks up - so the far mouth's tile is evened out into one, its corners lowered the way Level land lowers them (dragging the land around along). Extra keys as plan_bridge, plus corners (corner -> new height, evening out the far mouth: see apply_level) and trees (tiles that change shape and lose their trees). hint: when there's no way out, look further up the slope for a hillside that has one.

    Parameter
    • m: WorldMap
    • kind: String
    • a: Vector2i
    • hint: bool = true

  • Pathfinder.find static funcReturns {"tiles": Array[Vector2i], "end_heading": int} or {} when there is no route.
    Link zu diesem Eintragstatic func find(m: WorldMap, kind: String, start: Vector2i, heading: int, goals: Dictionary, allow_reverse_start: bool, allow_dead_end_uturn: bool, wired: bool = false, obey_signals: bool = true, avoid: Dictionary = {}) -> Dictionary

    A route that took a search also carries "box": every tile the search looked at lies inside it, so as long as the network doesn't change in there the same search gives the same route. goals: Dictionary of goal tiles. heading -1 means any first move is allowed. wired: an electric train, which can only run under overhead wires. obey_signals false: as if one-way signals let trains through both ways (to tell the player when they are what stands in the way). avoid: track blocks (ids of WorldMap.blocks) to keep off, where other trains are (RAIL-80).

    Link zu diesem Eintragstatic func _find_water(m: WorldMap, start: Vector2i, goals: Dictionary) -> Dictionary

    Ships turn where they like and sail a straight course afterwards (Vehicle.water_course), so this is the eight-way way of find_sea with each diagonal step split in two: a search over tiles rather than tiles and headings, with a heuristic that fits open water. Remembered on the map (see _sea_memo).

    Parameter

  • Pathfinder.find_sea static funcThe shortest way by water from start to goal, moving between tiles in eight directions (diagonally only where both tiles beside the step are water too), or [] when there is none.
    Link zu diesem Eintragstatic func find_sea(m: WorldMap, start: Vector2i, goal: Vector2i, max_len: float = INF) -> Array[Vector2i]

    Ships pull it straight afterwards (Vehicle.water_course): unlike the four-way route, it already runs close to the direct line, so the pulled course doesn't keep the corners of an L. max_len: ways longer than this don't count, which keeps the search to the water near the straight line (an answer of "none" then comes quickly even on a big sea).

    Parameter
    • m: WorldMap
    • start: Vector2i
    • goal: Vector2i
    • max_len: float = INF
    Rückgabewert
    Array[Vector2i]
    Deklariert in scripts/sim/pathfinder.gd:127

    A* over (tile, entry direction, shape), where shape remembers the turning tiles just behind: 0 straight track 1, 2 one turn so far, to the right / to the left 3, 4 two alternating turns, the last to the right / left 5, 6 three or more: a diagonal Open ground costs the same everywhere here (the rough pass has weighed up trees and slopes), which is what lets the search run straight to the goal. weight: 1 for the best line, more to settle sooner for a good one. Dateioptionen

Bei Feldnamen zählt die Groß- und Kleinschreibung. Die verlinkten Abschnitte erklären die Dateien mit Beispielen.

Datei oder AbschnittPflichtfelderOptionale Felder
mod.jsonidname, version, author, description
data.json → vehicles.<id>name, kind, cargos, speed, cost und run. Verwende look oder model sowie max_wagons für Loks oder cap für andere Fahrzeuge.desc, year, rel, electric, steam, length
data.json → cargo.<id>Vorhandene Fracht-IDrate, days
data.json → town_namesKeineprefixes, suffixes, replace
data.json → company_namesNamenslisteKeine
maps/<name>.jsonKeinename, description, settings

In settings sind w und h (64, 128, 256, 512, 1024), year (1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000) sowie towns, industries, rough und water (Indizes 0–3) möglich. rough reicht von flach bis bergig. Bei water folgen auf niedrig die Stufen normal, hoch und Inseln.

Der Wahrheitswert steam aktiviert Dampfeffekte und das Fahrverhalten für Dampfloks. length gibt die Länge eines eigenen Modells in Feldern an.

Das Dictionary Sim.options enthält die Simulationsoptionen cost, blocking, ai_level, max_loan, depots, breakdowns und goal. Karten-Mods verwenden die oben aufgeführten Felder unter settings.
